messages.subject: GSOC 2016
messages.body_plain:
Dear GSOC mentors,

As co-administrator for the R project participation in GSOC, I am currently writing the org application for R (due next Friday Feb 19).

One of the criteria that Google will use to evaluate our application is the number of mentors and projects available. Thus it would be great if mentors could already start posting project ideas to this year's wiki table https://github.com/rstats-gsoc/gsoc2016/wiki/table-of-proposed-coding-projects

There are currently a few projects already posted, and I encourage mentors to post their ideas as soon as possible. Please follow the template https://github.com/rstats-gsoc/gsoc2016/wiki/MENTORS%3A-Copy-this-template!

Thanks in advance and have a nice day!

Toby Dylan Hocking

messages.subject: Possible project idea - looking for mentors
messages.subject_clean: Possible project idea - looking for mentors
messages.body_plain:
Hi! I'm a graduate student in computer science. I'm looking for potential mentors and/or advice on my idea below:

Designing an R package for the creation of model evaluation curves. This would include both learning curves and validation curves.

When writing research, I often need to create learning curves to demonstrate the bias/variance tradeoff of a model, and I haven't found any package that addresses this. I also think validation curves would be interesting to include.

Hi,

we from mlr might be interested. But a few comments:

1) We had a very succesful gosc 2015 project on model visualization. I added Zach in CC who worked on this and the mentors.

2) mlr _already_ supports learning curves. See here:
http://mlr-org.github.io/mlr-tutorial/devel/html/learning_curve/index.html

3) What do you mean by "validation" curves (a somewhat fuzzy term).

In summary:
We have a lot of interest in model visualization, and quite a lot of code already in place. If you could write down a somewhat more detailed outline what you wanna do, we could talk.

Best

Bernd

Hi, I am reading the project wiki page and get confused about the goals in Description and Test.
In Description it mentions students will work on
> replacing the various time series charts in PerformanceAnalytics, PortfolioAnalytics, and quantmod with xts::plot.xts
and other functions regarding charting functionality.

As for the Test, the third point says students should provide a complete code example that could be used in PerformanceAnalytics pkg.
But it does not need to pertain to the subject of this project.
So, from my understanding, does it mean that we can create a function not based on xts::plot.xts?  And we will create a function under the PerformanceAnalytics pkg instead of
building a new package?

Many thanks in advance:)

On Monday, February 29, 2016 at 3:51:44 PM UTC-6, Eric Hung wrote:
> Hi, I am reading the project wiki page and get confused about the goals in Description and Test.
> In Description it mentions students will work on
> > replacing the various time series charts in PerformanceAnalytics, PortfolioAnalytics, and quantmod with xts::plot.xts
> and other functions regarding charting functionality.
>
> As for the Test, the third point says students should provide a complete code example that could be used in PerformanceAnalytics pkg.
> But it does not need to pertain to the subject of this project.
> So, from my understanding, does it mean that we can create a function not based on xts::plot.xts?  And we will create a function under the PerformanceAnalytics pkg instead of
> building a new package?
>

The project aims to *use* plot.xts to replace many of the existing plot functions in PerformanceAnalytics and other packages.  All the current charting functions in PerformanceAnalytics and quantmod use base graphics, and we'd like them updated to use the newer plot.xts functionality.  Additionally, there would be opportunities to extend plot.xts, for example via saving of plot specifications that could be reapplied to different data sets.

So, for a test, it would be best to choose an existing chart function of some complexity that could be reworked to use plot.xts.

We do not anticipate creating new packages with this project, just improving existing ones.

Regards,

Brian

messages.subject: Re: Possible project idea - looking for mentors
messages.subject_clean: Possible project idea - looking for mentors
messages.body_plain:
Thanks for the note! Let me provide more specific details and clarity on my idea:

Situation: many of the common model visualization / model evaluation plots either require lots of boilerplate code to visualize or are sparsely implemented across packages
e.g. learning curves are implemented in sklearn but you need to write the boilerplate code yourself to visualize; caret provides a means to plot the performance of tuning parameters (http://topepo.github.io/caret/training.html) but doesn't provide many of the other options provided by mlr; mlr provides the performance of tuning parameters but doesn't automatically generate curves.

Overall goal: provide easy to use methods for many of the common model visualization / evaluation plots

Quickly looking at what's available in mlr, here are some of my ideas to add (I am not an expert on the needs/features of the mlr codebase, so I'm happy to incorporate any ideas/feedback from you and the team):

Plotting a tuning parameter against the output of a scoring function (this is what I meant above by validation curve) - we use this on my team frequently especially for evaluating clustering (ie k in k-means) and dimensionality reduction. As discussed above, this could leverage the already implemented $opt.path.
Training/prediction time curves (depending on eager/lazy learner). This could potentially leverage the already implemented $opt.path but may need to be spit based on the type of learner.
Model complexity curves (ie plotting # of non-zero coefficients against the output of a scoring function)
Model visualization on pca-reduced data to visualize separation boundaries or highly dimensional data in 2D
Support for std bands for learning curves and any other model eval visualizations where a mean is calculated over several CV iterations for the scoring function
Support for epochs instead of train size (ie for neural nets) for applicable model visualizations
All model eval visualizations would ideally include "benchmarking", such as sklearn's Dummy model (looks like this is referenced issue #712 on github)

Best,
Mason
